candidate.listingDescription:
Download one ZIP for all three designs. Each comes in A4 (210 × 297 mm) and A3 (297 × 420 mm), giving you six vector PDFs to print yourself. The ZIP also contains a printing guide and a font notice. You supply the paper and frame.

In Phase portrait, follow a single navy line past three copper dots. Harmonic sum shows a smooth wave approaching a square wave in four steps. In Wave field, two waves cross to form a fine mesh.

Choose the file that matches your paper and print at actual size. The ivory background prints with the artwork. Colours can vary with the paper and printer.

editorial.reading:
21 November 2026 · AI reader critique of private edition 18d06477efdf

I would hang Phase portrait. The navy line crosses the centre and loops back through three copper dots. I can recognise its shape in the gallery before I can read the formula. Harmonic sum rewards a closer look. The four rows show a wave approaching a square, but its first label reads “01 terms”. Wave field looks like woven cloth at full size. At gallery size its fine lines merge and the shallow band feels small beside the other two prints.

I expect one digital download to print myself. The button says “Download the six PDFs”, so I expected six separate links. I opened the ZIP and found all three designs in both A4 and A3, a printing guide and a font notice. I would lead with Phase portrait and say “one ZIP” before describing the maths. Correct the first Harmonic sum label to “01 term” in both sizes. A physical A4 proof would settle how well the finest Wave field lines hold up on paper.

This is one AI editorial reading. The project has no independent customer response or purchase-intent evidence from this review.
